extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning, covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.publisher: York University, Nanyang Technological University, Salesforce Research
extraction.citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv:2203.10244.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, The Pew Research Center, Our World In Data (OWID), and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). For Pew, only chart images were crawled. For the other three, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid questions generated by the T5 model were filtered out if the answer could not be found in the chart data table.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts from Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD. Human-written chart summaries from Statista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Generated 23,111 questions automatically from human-written chart summaries using a T5 model. Filtered out invalid questions where the answer could not be found in the chart data table. Manually cleaned the test set of the machine-generated dataset by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and text descriptions. Extracted bounding boxes information of chart elements from SVG files. Extended ChartOCR pipeline to extract fully-structured data tables by associating data values with text labels using positional and color information. Used CRAFT model for text recognition.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA pairs were collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were asked to provide two questions (compositional and visual) per chart with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If answers matched exactly, they were considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual check on 500 random samples showed agreement of 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers were selected with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000. They were paid $0.6 USD per task based on the US minimum wage of $7.25 USD per hour.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Anonymized annotator data. Charts cover topics including social issues, demographic trends, and public opinion.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Models can be abused to mislead the public about the charts content and implications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Topic distribution is skewed; Politics is a common topic, particularly in the Pew dataset (45.4% U.S. Politics & Policy). Bar charts are the most common type of chart across all datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models cannot effectively handle nested arithmetic operations. Performance decreases when the gold data table is not provided due to automatic data extraction errors. OCR errors affect performance. Questions exhibit informal language and typos. Lower accuracy on line and dot line charts, logarithmic-scale charts, and pie charts.
